axes.model_access:
**A hybrid surface** — local models (GGUF download/management, llama.cpp-lineage backend) + cloud-model access
(OpenAI/Anthropic and similar API keys); four product lines: Studio (the desktop flagship) / Go (mobile) / Nexus (private enterprise LLM platform) / Stack (cloud-hosted).
axes.local_files: Reads and writes local files — local model files, chat history (local storage is its headline privacy positioning).
axes.background: The desktop app is persistent; the cloud lines (Stack/Nexus) involve a cloud account. Hybrid architecture: local inference does not depend on the cloud; cloud-model access needs an account/key.
axes.tools: In-app RAG/knowledge bases (document Q&A), an MCP access surface (per the official product-line wording); not a tool-plugging surface for agents — it is a consumer/enterprise desktop app.
axes.context:
In-app chat history persists locally; knowledge bases (RAG document libraries) are reused across sessions.
Context length varies with the chosen model and configuration (local models are bound by the llama.cpp-lineage backend's parameters).
axes.permissions: Desktop-app permissions = local files + network; the cloud lines need an account and subscription. Closed-source — no code-audit surface; privacy positioning follows the official site's self-description.
axes.fit:
Fits: wanting "one desktop app for local + cloud" hybrid use; private enterprise LLMs (the Nexus line).
Does not fit: open-source auditable stacks (closed-source); CLI-only serving routes (the vLLM/TGI line).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/runner/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/runner/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- Free/paid boundaries and quotas per product line (the pricing page not verified item by item)
- The bundled llama.cpp backend version and quant-tier support (closed-source; the version ships with the app)
- What the MCP access surface actually supports and how it is configured (mentioned in official product-line wording, not measured)
related: Same family: desktop GUI local-model apps; LM Studio is free closed-source, Msty leans heavier on hybrid cloud + enterprise lines.
Same family: the open-source desktop GUI Jan contrasted with the closed-source desktop GUI Msty.
Backend contrast: desktop GUI apps mostly ride a llama.cpp/Ollama-style local inference backend.
Hybrid-surface contrast: Msty connects local and cloud models in one app; ChatGPT has only the cloud line — the hybrid trade-off (one entry, two data boundaries) is exactly its product claim.
sources: Msty · official site (live domain msty.ai returned 200 direct; product matrix Studio/Go/Nexus/Stack; CloudStack, LLC)
